body: A one-minute explainer on Delhi's smog. Air-quality readings in Delhi, Noida and Gurugram passed 450 before dawn on Monday, the worst of the season so far. Doctors advise people with breathing problems to stay indoors, and the city's emergency rules stop building work, keep diesel trucks out of Delhi and ask offices to let staff work from home where they can. A correction says only Delhi's primary schools moved online; schools in Noida and Gurugram remain open. Not confirmed: how long Delhi's primary schools stay online (the Monday update said until Friday; the correction doesn't say).

media.transcript:
This is an illustrative sample made from Hrizzup's example story. Delhi's air has turned severe.

Before dawn on Monday, AQI readings in Delhi, Noida and Gurugram passed 450, the worst of the season so far. Doctors advise people with breathing problems to stay indoors.

The emergency rules stop building work, keep diesel trucks out of Delhi, and ask offices to let staff work from home where they can.

Schools changed twice. On Monday, an update said schools across Delhi NCR had moved online until Friday. On Tuesday, a correction said only Delhi's primary schools have. Schools in Noida and Gurugram remain open.

What isn't confirmed is how long Delhi's primary schools stay online. The correction doesn't say.

Sources are in the post.

still.description: A tall white picture. At the top, a drawing in flat colours of three school buildings side by side under a hazy sky: the one on the left has an open laptop on its roof like a hat and a shut door; the other two have lit windows and open doors. Under the drawing, in tall black capital letters: "DELHI'S AIR TURNS SEVERE". Under that, in smaller bold type: "An illustrative one-minute explainer". At the bottom right, in small bold type: "Illustrative sample".
